brief: GS's weekly Asia tech/positioning note: hot CPI revived Fed-hike debate though October looks like a hold; CXMT's claimed memory breakthrough triggered a Korea memory sell-off that spilled into global tech, reviving scrutiny of AI capex sustainability, ROIC and funding. GS's Global AI basket selling over Oct 8-15 matched the late-July episode and was the largest since March 2022, though positioning (6/10 on length) is cleaner than June/July; unlike July's technical unwind, this episode opened a genuine fundamentals debate. Asia Tech, previously richer-positioned than the US, bore the brunt: its share of Global Net MV fell to 18% from a 27% June peak. GS sold $7.8bn net in Asia (Taiwan -$2.75bn, China -$2.1bn, Japan -$1.9bn, Korea -$700m); outside GS, Taiwan saw record FII selling (-$19.2bn) while Korea, already de-risked (over $110bn FII selling since May), looks cleaner. KOSPI's eight-day >20% drop matches crisis-era declines, which GS reads as favorable risk-reward for a tactical bounce. GS downplays CXMT's ability to close the technology gap given 4F2's manufacturing complexity. Elsewhere, momentum unwound into quality: Europe and India outperformed, and US markets rotated to defensives.
